quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving on rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, which group formation is best?

options.text: Pairs.
Single-file.
Staggered.
Passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straightaways, but switch to single-file when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left of your lane.
Do not worry about your position in the lane.
Always ride on the far right of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stay visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding with you?

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control and hold onto passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually found?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down somewhere drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down somewhere drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing where drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, why should you rise slightly off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if you need to.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does the front brake do?

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of your total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It means turning off the engine to slow down.
It means slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It is not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows down your motorcycle. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Before you carry a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This lets you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders behind them can watch them closely.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it harder to see.
Stay in only one lane position.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: How much attention does a motorcycle need?

options.text: Less frequent attention than a car.
More frequent attention than a car.
Pre-ride checks should only be done by a mechanic.
It should only be serviced at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent attention than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Small problems can be more serious on a motorcycle. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: To stay in control while turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be prepared to avoid hazards.

questions.question: A motorist on an entrance ramp to your right may not see you. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move to another lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles entering from an entrance ramp. Move to a lane farther from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to safely enter.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view so you can focus better.
You will have more time to react to what others do.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what others do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around problems.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.
Not weave between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Riding between slow or parked cars is dangerous. Car doors may open, or cars may suddenly move into traffic. You will not have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Not ride during the day.
Choose safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, make yourself visible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Stay flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay close to the vehicle ahead by reducing your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Always be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies in poor conditions.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open.
